newsitem.title: USA: GM reduces Q3 N. American production plan.
newsitem.headline: GM reduces Q3 N. American production plan.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Friday it reduced its third quarter North American production schedule by 20,000 vehicles because of production losses from recent strikes in Pontiac and Warren, Mich.

GM said it now expects to build 1,288,000 cars and trucks in the United States, Canada and Mexico during the third quarter, which represents a 2.4 percent increase over the 1,258,000 North American vehicles it built in the third quarter of 1996.
In July, GM said it built 259,000 cars and trucks in North America, compared with 308,000 a year earlier.
GM's July car production totaled 143,000 units, down from 167,000 a year earlier, while July truck production totaled 116,000 units, down from 141,000 a year earlier.

For the third quarter as a whole, the latest forecast subtracted about 14,000 cars from plans released a month ago, bringing GM's car output for the July-September period to 700,000 units. GM also plans to produce about 6,000 fewer trucks, bringing its current forecast for the quarter to 14,000 units.

GM suffered a three-month strike at its Pontiac, Mich., full-size pickup truck plant which ended July 18, and a six-day strike ended July 27 at a plant in Warren, Mich., that produces car transmissions, wheels and suspension parts.
The automaker faces another strike deadline of 1159 EDT Friday/0359 GMT Saturday at its Cadillac assembly plant in the Detroit enclave of Hamtramck, Mich.
Talks aimed at averting a strike and reaching a new local labor agreement for the plant were expected to continue all day Friday.
